Megastudy of 6000 words

Source: R/data.R
megastudy.Rd

Item-level norms for 6000 words, as in large lexical decision megastudies: mean RT and accuracy per word, with correlated lexical predictors. For multiple regression, collinearity, non-linear effects and variable importance.

Usage

megastudy

Format

A tibble with 6000 rows and 9 columns:

word

Word ID, w0001 to w6000.

log_freq

log10 frequency per million words.

length

Length in letters, 2 to 15.

syllables

Number of syllables, 1 to 6.

neighbours

Number of orthographic neighbours.

aoa

Age of acquisition in years.

concreteness

Concreteness rating, 1 to 5.

rt

Mean lexical decision RT in ms.

accuracy

Proportion of correct responses.

Source

data-raw/megastudy.R

Details

True model:

rt = 825 - 120 * plogis(log_freq - 2.5) + 9 * (length - 7)
  + 8 * (syllables - 2.5) - 2 * neighbours + 10 * (aoa - 7)
  - 6 * (concreteness - 3) + e
accuracy = plogis(2.5 + 0.7 * (log_freq - 2.5) - 0.2 * (aoa - 7) + e)

The error e is normal with SD 35 ms for RT and SD 0.5 for accuracy. The frequency effect is S-shaped: it levels off for very rare and very frequent words. Frequent words are shorter, have more neighbours and are acquired earlier. Syllables correlate with length (r = 0.75): on its own, each syllable adds about 39 ms, but only 8 ms once length is in the model. Mean length (8 letters), mean number of syllables (2.6), mean RT (about 790 ms) and mean accuracy (0.86) are close to the English Lexicon Project words (Balota et al. 2007: 8 letters, 2.54 syllables, 784 ms, 0.84), but RTs vary less across words (SD 68 ms against 135 ms). In the English Lexicon Project, the number of syllables has an inhibitory effect of its own and the length effect is U-shaped (New et al. 2006); here the length effect is linear. The effects and data are simulated.

References

Balota, D. A., Yap, M. J., Cortese, M. J., Hutchison, K. A., Kessler, B., Loftis, B., Neely, J. H., Nelson, D. L., Simpson, G. B. & Treiman, R. (2007). The English Lexicon Project. Behavior Research Methods, 39(3), 445-459. doi:10.3758/BF03193014

New, B., Ferrand, L., Pallier, C. & Brysbaert, M. (2006). Reexamining the word length effect in visual word recognition: New evidence from the English Lexicon Project. Psychonomic Bulletin & Review, 13(1), 45-52. doi:10.3758/BF03193811

Examples

round(cor(megastudy[c("log_freq", "length", "syllables", "neighbours", "aoa")]), 2)
#>            log_freq length syllables neighbours   aoa
#> log_freq       1.00  -0.41     -0.30       0.25 -0.57
#> length        -0.41   1.00      0.75      -0.63  0.24
#> syllables     -0.30   0.75      1.00      -0.46  0.18
#> neighbours     0.25  -0.63     -0.46       1.00 -0.15
#> aoa           -0.57   0.24      0.18      -0.15  1.00
coef(lm(rt ~ syllables, data = megastudy))
#> (Intercept)   syllables 
#>   686.68015    38.95821 
m1 <- lm(rt ~ log_freq + length + syllables + neighbours + aoa + concreteness,
         data = megastudy)
m2 <- lm(rt ~ splines::ns(log_freq, 4) + length + syllables + neighbours + aoa +
           concreteness, data = megastudy)
anova(m1, m2)
#> Analysis of Variance Table
#> 
#> Model 1: rt ~ log_freq + length + syllables + neighbours + aoa + concreteness
#> Model 2: rt ~ splines::ns(log_freq, 4) + length + syllables + neighbours + 
#>     aoa + concreteness
#>   Res.Df     RSS Df Sum of Sq      F    Pr(>F)    
#> 1   5993 7286785                                  
#> 2   5990 7241395  3     45390 12.515 3.728e-08 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
coef(m2)[c("length", "syllables", "neighbours", "aoa", "concreteness")]
#>       length    syllables   neighbours          aoa concreteness 
#>     8.861030     8.142864    -1.992065     9.643519    -6.460866
